title: Bridge Hire: 10-Day Rapid Assimilation & Shadow Rotation Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This playbook is a lightweight, pragmatic plan for rapid absorption of a bridge (backfill or short-notice) hire into a product pod. It trades breadth for speed: the goal is to reach contributor-level confidence on high-priority tasks within 10 calendar days while preserving psychological safety and knowledge continuity.

Scope and when to use this playbook:
- For backfills where time-to-impact matters more than a full 90-day ramp (e.g., critical feature velocity, on-call coverage).
- For lateral transfers or contractor-to-perm conversions where prior experience exists but product/context knowledge is limited.
- Not a replacement for full role onboarding — follow-up 30/60/90 planning should be scheduled after day 10.

High-level timeline (10-day sprint):
- Day -1 / Offer accepted: Invitation + pre-boarding pack (Slack, access requests, org chart, first-week goals).
- Day 0: Welcome, baseline admin, team introductions, high-level product orientation.
- Days 1–3: Shadow rotations with primary mentor + two hands-on micro-tasks.
- Days 4–6: Paired work on triage tickets and one small feature/bug with code reviews.
- Days 7–9: Independent ownership of a small deliverable; run a short async demo.
- Day 10: Readout + calibration with hiring manager and mentor, go/no-go signals and next steps.

Hiring-plan checklist (pre-boarding to Day 0):
- Hiring manager: finalize top 3 impact areas the role must cover in first 30 days.
- People Ops: confirm title, comp paperwork, start date, and remote/home-office stipend.
- IT/Security: pre-provision laptop image, VPN, KMS access, and Okta groups.
- Mentor (peer): assigned and calendar blocked for first 10 days.
- Prepare two starter tickets (one onboarding, one small feature/bug) with clear acceptance criteria.

Interview rubric (compact, role-agnostic template for fast calibration):
Scoring: 1-4 (1 = insufficient, 4 = excellent). Add notes and example evidence.
- Technical/Role Skill (score): domain skills, ability to ship small features.
- Problem Solving (score): debugging approach, triage clarity, tradeoffs.
- Collaboration & Communication (score): cross-functional clarity, async docs.
- Ownership & Reliability (score): past examples of shipping under ambiguity.
- Security & Compliance Awareness (score): basic awareness for Redwood context.
Interviewers should record 1–2 bullet example evidence per competency and an overall risk rating (low/medium/high).

Shadow rotation playbook (days 1–3):
- Goal: expose the hire to common flows, code paths, and people.
- Daily structure: 30m mentor 1:1 (standup + context), 3h shadowing/reading, 2–3h paired work.
- Topics to cover: local dev setup, CI pipeline, observability dashboards, recent incident postmortem, high-priority feature code path.
- Deliverable by end of day 3: annotated notes + one queued PR ready for review.

10-Day Operational Checklist (short actionable items):
Day 0 (Welcome):
- Create Slack intro post + pin org chart.
- Confirm laptop + VPN access.
- Walk through first-week goals and required meetings.

Days 1–3 (Shadow):
- Complete secure-coding checklist and sign-off.
- Pair on onboarding ticket; open PR template.
- Save three troubleshooting commands/processes to personal notes.

Days 4–6 (Pair-to-own):
- Triage two customer-facing tickets with mentor.
- Own a small bug/feature end-to-end (branch, tests, PR).
- Add one note to team runbook where a gap was encountered.

Days 7–9 (Independent delivery):
- Launch small deliverable to staging and run basic smoke tests.
- Deliver short async demo in team channel with key learnings.
- Feedback loop: 1:1 with hiring manager and mentor mid-block.

Day 10 (Calibration):
- Readout doc: accomplishments, open risks, blockers, next 30-day objectives.
- Risk assessment: green/yellow/red and proposed mitigations.
- Schedule follow-up 30/60/90 planning session.

Success signals (what good looks like at day 10):
- Can run and validate a local change and create a reasonable PR without heavy hand-holding.
- Demonstrates clear communication on ticket status and triage decisions.
- Identified at least one actionable runbook improvement or automation.
- Mentor and manager alignment: low/medium risk and a clear path to full productivity.

Handoff template for outgoing to incoming (if backfill):
- One-paragraph role summary + three current priorities.
- Top five artifacts (dashboards, runbooks, key PRs/commits) with short context notes.
- Recurring meetings (who, cadence, why) and any pending blocking decisions.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Failure: Overloading with context => Mitigate: prioritize 3 core flows and defer secondary docs.
- Failure: No mentor bandwidth => Mitigate: assign rotational backup + async buddy notes.
- Failure: Lack of clear starter tasks => Mitigate: pre-create micro-tasks with clear acceptance criteria.

Templates and micro-formats (copyable):
- 1-line daily status for the new hire: "Yesterday I X; Today I Y; Blockers Z."
- PR checklist snippet: "Does this include tests? Did I update runbook? Has security tag been considered?"
- 10-day readout template headings: Accomplishments, Open Items, Risks & Mitigations, Next 30d Focus.

Next steps after day 10:
- Schedule a 30/60/90 planning session with manager and mentor.
- Add hire to regular onboarding cohort demo to expose cross-team context.
- Transfer ownership of long-running knowledge transfer items to mentor with defined deadlines.

Notes to People Ops and hiring managers:
- This is an acceleration playbook, not a shortcut for skipping compliance or security gates. All mandatory trainings and paperwork must be completed by the end of day 3.
- Keep the first two weeks focused on a few concrete outcomes; measure signals not feelings.

Revision log: Draft v0.1 (2025-03-10) created by Aisha Patel; updated v0.2 (2025-03-18) with interview rubric compacting and added shadow rotation timings.
